definitions.explanation: The row or line at the back, whether of seats, people, or a formation.

examples.japanese: {後列|こうれつ}に{座|すわ}った。
examples.english: I sat in the back row.

examples.japanese: {後列|こうれつ}からは{舞台|ぶたい}が{見|み}えにくい。
examples.english: It's hard to see the stage from the back row.

examples.japanese: {背|せ}の{高|たか}い{人|ひと}は{後列|こうれつ}に{回|まわ}ってもらえると、{前|まえ}の{人|ひと}が{見|み}やすくなります。
examples.english: If taller people move to the back row, it will be easier for those in front to see.

notes:
A straightforward compound of {後|こう} (back, rear) + {列|れつ} (row, line). The counterpart of {前列|ぜんれつ} (front row).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {後列|こうれつ}の{席|せき}: back row seat
- {最後列|さいこうれつ}: the very back row
- {後列|こうれつ}に{並|なら}ぶ: to line up in the back row
- {後列|こうれつ}に{移動|いどう}する: to move to the back row

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {前列|ぜんれつ}: front row — the antonym
- {後方|こうほう}: the rear (area) — refers to a general area, not a specific row
- {最後尾|さいこうび}: the very end of a line — specifically the tail of a queue

cross_references.label: the very end of a line
